subject: Function orchestration — SDK setup, auth & parallel tool patterns (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@finex.co>, Rajiv Kumar <rajiv.kumar@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Function orchestration — SDK setup, auth & parallel tool patterns (post-call recap)

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Great speaking with you both earlier. Quick recap from our discovery + the technical follow-ups we discussed. I tried to capture the integration and architecture items you flagged so the engineering team has a clear set of next steps.

Key takeaways from today's call:
- Primary flow: front-end sends an authorization request -> Redwood routes to model for structured extraction -> model calls two tools in parallel (merchant_enrichment, risk_scoring) -> orchestrator combines outputs -> final structured JSON sent back to app.
- Sensitivity: this is PCI-adjacent (transaction metadata + PII). You indicated that tokens with card PANs are redacted upstream; we still recommend mTLS and short-lived tokens for service-to-service auth.
- SLA & routing: low-latency path for auth flows (99th pct latency target <150ms). For non-critical enrichment jobs we can route to a lower-cost path.

Architectural recommendations (high level):
1) SDK & bootstrap
   - Use Redwood SDK (Python/Node/Go) for request signing and streaming; SDK handles KV cache keys and continuous batching out-of-the-box.
   - Provide a small wrapper in your service to add idempotency keys and request metadata (customer_id, correlation_id).

2) Auth options (recommended order)
   - mTLS + short-lived JWT for S2S calls (recommended for Prod). Use your KMS to mint service JWTs; Redwood can accept customer certs in Private deployments.
   - Managed API keys with rotation + signed headers for Hosted PoC. Keys should be limited scope and rotated monthly.

3) Tool/function calling pattern
   - Define tools as typed endpoints with explicit input/output schemas (json-schema). Example tools: merchant_enrichment, risk_scoring, pricing_lookup.
   - Invoke tools in parallel when independent and combine with a lightweight aggregator in the orchestrator.
   - Use timeouts + circuit breaker per tool (suggest 120–300ms for risk/merchant lookups; fallback to cached values).
   - Error handling: surface tool errors in structured_response.errors array and include retryable flag. For non-critical enrichment failures, return the response with a "partial" flag and a trace_id for later reprocessing.

4) Structured output and model constraints
   - Use structured output mode (model returns a validated JSON object). Keep the schema strict for production (avoid free-form text for fields used downstream).
   - Use tool calling for authoritative data (do not have the model invent merchant IDs).

5) Embeddings & reranker notes
   - Two options for embedding store: hosted embeddings (Redwood-managed vectors for PoC) or customer-managed vector DB (e.g., Milvus/Elastic/Weaviate) behind your VPC for scale/compliance.
   - For reranking, precompute candidate embeddings and run lightweight distance-based filter before model rerank to save tokens. We recommend a 2-stage approach: vector shortlist -> model-based rerank with smaller context.

Next steps / asks for your team:
- Confirm whether you prefer a PoC with Redwood-hosted embeddings or a VPC-hosted vector DB.
- Share the SOC2 contact for a security questionnaire (Laura will follow up).
- Can we schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive (Karthik + Laura + your infra lead) next week? I proposed Tue or Thu mornings PT — open to alternatives.

Attachments: redwood-integ-arch-v1.pdf (diagram), sdk-auth-sample.txt (minimal snippets), auth-flow.drawio.png

Thanks,

Dev Patel

Subject: Re: Function orchestration — SDK setup, auth & parallel tool patterns (post-call recap)

Elena — great questions, answered inline below. Karthik and Laura are on-copy for deeper technical/security details during the deep-dive.

1) Embeddings migration path
   - Yes. Redwood-hosted embeddings are intended for quick PoCs. We expose a snapshot/export API that produces a compressed archive of vectors + ids, and a small mapping manifest for re-ingestion into customer vector DBs. We also publish a CLI helper that imports into Milvus/Weaviate/Elastic.

2) KMS/HSM integration and token verification
   - For Hosted API: Redwood can accept JWTs signed by your external KMS as long as we have the public key / JWKS endpoint. That's the simplest for customers who want to keep signing keys in their KMS.
   - For Private/VPC: you can bring your certs and we can terminate mTLS at the customer edge (we support mutual TLS with client cert validation). Laura — I think we should include the KMS acceptance matrix in our security reply (SOC2 artifact).

3) SDK samples & patterns
   - Attached sdk-auth-sample.txt has two short snippets showing: (a) function/tool definitions with json-schema; (b) an example orchestrator that fires two async requests (merchant_enrichment, risk_scoring) and awaits both with per-call timeouts + circuit-breaker.
   - Pattern guidance: keep tool implementations idempotent and return a stable canonical id for each enrichment so retries are safe. Use a correlation_id for tracing.

4) Function calling / error handling patterns (concrete)
   - Fan-out: start both calls in parallel with Promise.allSettled / asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True). If merchant_enrichment fails but risk_scoring succeeds, return the risk result and mark enrichment as "partial".
   - Timeouts: enforce server-side timeouts slightly shorter than client SLA to avoid cascading latency. Example: client SLA 150ms, per-tool timeout 120ms.
   - Circuit-breaker: track error rate & latency; open the circuit for the specific tool if failures exceed threshold; fall back to cached responses for a short window.
   - Observability: attach tool-level traces and include token-level cost & latency breakdowns in logs so you can tune batching/quantization.

5) Structured output enforcement
   - We recommend schema-first: register the json-schema with the model route and enable strict validation (reject responses that violate required fields). For fields that come from tools, mark them as authoritative in the schema so the orchestrator trusts those values.

Proposed deep-dive: Tue 30 Mar 2026, 10:00 AM PT — 60 min. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda (SDK walkthrough, auth/KMS patterns, routing & fallback demo).

Laura — can you lead the short security notes and SOC2 questionnaire?

Thanks,

Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
